newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra sees slightly higher 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Metra sees slightly higher 1997 profit.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab said on Wednesday it expected earnings to improve slightly this year compared to 1996.
"Eliminating the impact of non-recurring items, the profit after net financial items is expected to increase slightly," Metra said in a statement with its 1996 results.
"Metra's consolidated net sales, including the NSD (New Sulzer Diesel) companies, are forecast to rise to 15 billion markka during 1997," it said.
Metra's 1996 profit after financial items was 894 million markka, up from 795 million. Net sales were 11.7 billion markka.
The group's operating profit including the earnings of associated companies was 1.08 billion markka, up from 1.00 billion, Metra said.

This included a non-recurring gain totalling 248 million markka, the most significant elements of which were a gain of 272 million markka on the disposal of Assa Abloy shares and a 98 million markka gain on the sale of the Hotel Strand property.
Metra said its recently formed Wartsila NSD unit's net sales are expected to exceed 11 billion markka, but restructuring costs mean its profits in relation to net sales would remain almost unchanged.
Metra's Wartsila Diesel unit's 1996 net sales were eight billion markka, up from 6.9 billion.
